mode: actual X11 screen capture of a dedicated Kitty window on an isolated Xvfb display; actual Neovim, Rust server, and Pi adapter
model: Pi faux provider with fixed responses; no provider credentials supplied
tools: actual Bash tool creates a stored child agent through the Rust command client; faux responses prescribe the tool call
input: keys sent to the terminal with Kitty remote control
capture: FFmpeg x11grab restricted to the terminal window

steps.text: Run ./harness.sh from your project. This test starts without a configuration file or key.
Press ;. The left tree lists agents from this directory. Select + New chat.
Press Enter. Chat history fills the normal file area. The small message box is below it.
Type \model and press Enter. The model list is scrollable and searchable.
Page Down scrolls the list. The footer shows your position and the total number of choices.
Press G to reach the last choice. Select Local demo with Enter for fixed replies without a key.
Type \name Review and press Enter. The name is optional; no name dialog blocks creation.
Write a task. Shift-Enter adds a line; Enter sends the complete prompt.
The actual Bash tool creates the child through the command client. The editor stays available.
Press Escape, then ; twice and r. Tests is nested under the Review agent that created it.
Select Tests with Enter. This child opens with an empty, separate conversation.
Press Escape, then Ctrl-^ to return to the previous chat. Native buffers hold each conversation.
Use :buffer app.py to return to the file. The message box closes; the file uses the full height.
Press Ctrl-^ to return to Review. The chat and its message box return in the same editor area.
Press p, then Escape. From the input, :vsplit app.py opens a file at normal height.
Click the conversation. Its input returns below that chat only; the file keeps its full height.
Press p, Escape, then :q. Only the input closes. The chat and file stay open.
The chats stay saved. Press Escape, then :qa to close the idle editor.
For AI coding, use \model to select Anthropic, then \login to enter your key.

assertions: no configuration file or credentials before startup
normal editor starts with one window
semicolon shows only New chat in the empty directory tree
Enter on New opens chat without setup or name dialogs
model list opens through a chat command and Page Down scrolls
G reaches the last choice and Enter selects the local demo
name is set through a local chat command
Shift-Enter inserts a line and Enter submits the prompt
actual Bash tool creates a child with the correct stored parent
child appears nested under its creator
child selection opens separate empty history
chat history occupies the normal file window
Ctrl-^ switches between chat buffers
buffer command opens the source file and hides the message box
Ctrl-^ returns to the prior chat and restores its message box
no configuration file is written by chat settings
vsplit from input opens a normal height file
mouse click on chat restores input only beneath that chat
q closes only the input and preserves chat and file
normal idle exit closes Neovim
cleanup: all demonstration sessions stopped; private server shut down; terminal closed
